enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
448 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

...New FIRE WEATHER...


.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 445 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

 - We will see cooler temperatures on Saturday and Sunday with
   highs running 3 to 5 degrees below average. 

 - There will be a chance for some light mountain rain or high
   elevation snow showers Saturday evening. 

 - Temperatures look to remain slightly below normal into next
   week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1040 PM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

An approaching upper level trough has brought moisture, rain and
lots of clouds to the area this evening. The thunderstorms will
continue to move off to the northeast and should clear the area a
little after midnight. On Saturday a second short wave will rotate
across New Mexico and bring some rain showers mainly to area 
mountains Saturday afternoon and evening. I wouldn't be surprised 
if there was some rain mixed with snow above 8K, but no snow 
accumulations are expected. In addition to the mountain 
precipitation, we will see breezy west winds across the region 
Saturday afternoon. For Sunday the upper level trough will be to 
our east while an upper level ridge will be building into the west
coast. This pattern will keep us dry, but cool. High temperatures
both Saturday and Sunday will run 3 to 5 degrees below average.

On Monday an upper level short wave ridge will dash across New
Mexico and that will keep us dry with less winds. Behind the ridge
another upper level trough will begin to get organized just off
the coast of California. As the trough approaches the area on 
Tuesday we will again see a chance for rain, mainly in area 
mountains. High temperatures both Monday and Tuesday, will run 
just a degree or two below average. For the end of next week, we 
will see yet another upper level trough begin to approach the 
region. Right now it looks like most of the precipitation will 
stay to north of our area so there are not a lot of precipitation
chances in the forecast. High temperatures for the end of the 
week will be near seasonal averages. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 423 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

Some lingering light rain showers looks to continue into the 
afternoon hours today. Models continue to suggest some low clouds 
and perhaps some fog across the area this morning but confidence is 
too low to mention in the TAFs. If it does occur, it will burn off 
soon after sunrise. Cloud coverage will slowly decrease through the 
day becoming much clearer after 00Z. Breezy west winds expected 
areawide with speeds generally 15-20G25-30KT. Winds will stay a 
little elevated after dark (10-15KT). 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 445 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

Low fire weather concerns through the week ahead. Min RH values stay 
above critical thresholds each day. Lingering light rain showers 
possible through the day today. Min RHs increase today to 40-60% in 
the lowlands and 70-100% in the area mountains. Min RHs decrease 
slightly again Sunday due to dry conditions. Min RHs increase 
slightly Monday and Tuesday with values of 40-60% in the lowlands 
and 60-80% in the area mountains. Models are suggesting the rain 
chances we were seeing previously for Tuesday are dwindling and may 
just be mostly breezy conditions with low-end rain chances possible.

20 foot winds will be breezy with speeds of 10-20 mph with gusts to 
35 mph. Sunday and onward, 20 foot winds remain light each day at 5-
10 mph. Temperatures stay below normal each day through mid-week 
next week.

&&
